tasks.title: Cross-request payment replay and requirement substitution are rejected
tasks.description: Threat model: settled payment evidence quoted against one PaymentRequirements set (price, recipient, asset, network, resource) must never authorise a different, more expensive or otherwise unauthorised request. The exact scheme binds amount, asset and payTo on chain, and the memo binds nonce uniqueness, but no scheme field cryptographically binds the protected resource; the verifier therefore enforces the binding at the trust boundary by recording the requirements hash a transaction was verified under and refusing the same transaction against any different requirements set. Fail closed on missing or malformed requirements. Acceptance criteria AC01-AC08 below are the required security outcomes; the formal core each sandbox check runs is deliberately small and does not bound the natural-language claim.

criteria.statement: F10 catches a verifier that accepts a settled payload against a different requirements set (cross-request replay)
A settled payment is rejected when re-verified against a higher-priced requirements set (amount escalation)
Evidence quoted for recipient A is rejected against requirements naming recipient B
Payment evidence bound to one resource's requirements is rejected against another resource's requirements even when amount and recipient match
Verification fails closed on missing or malformed requirements fields
A legitimate retry of the same request against the same requirements keeps the existing idempotency and duplicate-settlement contract
A valid new payment for the higher-priced request settles normally (no false positive against honest traffic)
The full offline suite, including every F1-F9 case, passes unchanged

tasks.title: R14: a crash between a successful /settle and the response
tasks.description: The probe kills the resource server after /settle succeeds and before the client gets the response, at two points (while /settle is answering, and as the first byte of the response arrives), restarts it and presents the same payment, with a payment-identifier id when the server advertises the extension. It passes only if, at both points, there is at most one settlement, the server never calls /settle again for that payment, never answers 402 to it, and either delivers once from an idempotency record or refuses naming the transaction, payment id, signature or nonce so the payment can be reconciled. Solana devnet and Base Sepolia (exact). Wired into the CLI (--crash, --crash-kill, --crash-restart), the Action (crash, crash-kill, crash-restart), the JSON, SARIF and JUnit reports and docs/FIXES.md. A reference server with a durable record passes; three faulty builds of it fail.
